You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
Key features: the policy rate is high relative to its 3-year average (+2.0), up from 12 months earlier (+2.0), and the 10-year yield is low relative to its history (-2.0). The unemployment rate z is -1.0 but up 2.0 over 12 months, so it is rising from a low base. Payrolls are weak. Core CPI is high. The dollar is down sharply over 12 months. Gold is very strong, with a 12-month z of +3.0.

This resembles late 2007 to early 2008 only loosely, because the policy rate's 12-month change of +2.0 doesn't fit. A better match is a period in which the Fed has hiked a lot and the 10-year yield is falling. Candidates are late 2024 or mid-2025.

For mid-2025, the policy rate z would be high at about +2 after the 2022-23 hikes, but the 12-month change in the rate would be about 0 or negative. A 12-month change of +2.0 in the policy rate points to the 2022-23 hiking period, but then the 10-year yield would not be -2 versus its 3-year average.

Consider 2007 instead. The 3-year window of 2004-07 includes the hikes, and the rate was up in the 12 months to mid-2006. Gold strength fits 2007. But the dollar was falling in 2007, which also fits, and the 12-month change in equities was negative, which does not.

Consider 2019 as a third option. The policy rate was high versus 2016-19, and the 12-month change was +2.0 as hikes ran through 2018. The 10-year yield fell sharply in 2019, and gold rose over the 6 and 12 months to August 2019. Equities were up 1m, 3m and 6m, but the 12m z of -1.0 fits a period that includes the Q4 2018 drop. The dollar's 12m z of -2.0 fits poorly with 2019, though.

Consider early 2019 again. In January or February 2019 the 10-year yield was falling and equities had rebounded. Gold's 12m z of +3 doesn't fit that well, though.

Consider 2024 as a fourth option. Core CPI at +2.0 and the policy rate at +2.0 fit, but the unemployment rate z would be higher. The 12-month policy rate change of +2.0 doesn't fit 2024 either.

Consider March 2020 or the 2020 window. A policy rate z of +2 doesn't fit because rates were cut.

For 2008, the policy rate would be falling, so that doesn't fit.

Perhaps early 2025? The 10y z would be about +1, so no.

The best remaining fit is 2019, around August to October. Unemployment low (-1.0), but up 2.0 over 12 months isn't right for 2019, since it was falling. That conflicts with the rising-unemployment reading.

Perhaps 2001? That is outside the 2007-2026 range.

Consider 2023-24 again, with the rate z at +2 and 12m +2.0: mid-2023. But the 10y z would be high then. The unemployment z of -1 with a +2.0 12m change fits 2022-23 more than the others, since unemployment was at record lows in 2022.

Settling on late 2019 as the compromise guess.

{"year":2019,"month":10,"confidence":0.2,"cues":["10y yield z -2 and falling while policy rate z +2 after hikes","gold 12m z +3 with weak payrolls","equities recovering after a negative 12m return"]}
